articles.title: Community Day draws 2,712 registrations across 35 countries
articles.dek: Ninety-seven events prompt a fresh look at meetup sizes and earlier planning for next year.
body: An average of 28 registrations per meetup has the foundation reconsidering its earlier suggestion of keeping gatherings below 20 people. Missy Quarry’s recap reports 76% more registered guests than last year and 20% more events.

This was the second annual Community Day and the first to include the ESPHome and Music Assistant communities. Hosts organized hardware swaps, presentations and music quizzes, alongside locally made gifts.

Support for hosts continues throughout the year, including eligible venue costs, host travel and meals, and custom merchandise or materials. The community team plans clearer guidance in its Meetups Playbook after questions about reimbursements and hosting exposed gaps.
The next Community Day is planned for the second half of 2027, with a save-the-date announcement expected in the first quarter. No exact event date has been announced.

articles.title: Know which switch you’re changing without seeing the screen
articles.dek: Automation fields and selected labels gain spoken names; choosing a dashboard card also works from the keyboard.
body: An unnamed checkbox gives no clue whether it selects a device, enables an optional action field or completes a task. Home Assistant gives those controls names that screen readers can announce, while label menus distinguish labels applied to all selected items from those applied to only some.

Each dashboard-card preview becomes one named button, reached with Tab and selected with Enter or Space. The controls inside the preview stay out of the way. On narrow settings pages, focus follows the visible order from the header through the content to the bottom tabs.

Address search during initial setup keeps focus in the search field and announces the selected place. Enter chooses a result without unexpectedly completing the step. Assist and entity-detail dialogs also gain spoken titles, completing a gap left in October’s ordinary-dialog changes.

articles.title: Find the meters missing from your energy dashboard
articles.dek: Suggestions cover electricity, gas and water, with a chance to review each choice before saving.
body: A meter can already be collecting statistics without appearing in the household energy picture. Home Assistant’s Energy settings lists those unused readings on the relevant tab, with options to add or dismiss them.

Choosing Add opens the appropriate editor with the meter selected. A reading that could fit several roles prompts a choice first, and nothing is saved until the editor is confirmed. Already configured meters and their related helper sources are skipped to avoid suggesting the same measurement twice.
Dismissed suggestions are remembered separately for each user.

articles.title: Two speakers, one stereo pair
articles.dek: Sendspin pairs share their volume and can join a larger speaker group.
body: Choose two compatible Sendspin speakers in player settings, assign left and right channels, and give the pair a name. The pair becomes one player in both Music Assistant and Home Assistant, with one volume control and shared sound processing.

Previously, assigning channels through a synchronized group left both speakers visible and prevented that pair from joining another group. The new pair can take part in a larger group. If one speaker goes offline, the other plays both channels until it returns; taking the pair apart restores the individual players.

articles.title: A way back online for boards with older radio firmware
articles.dek: The repair addresses a failure after the November update; ESP32-C5 owners also get a warning before a risky firmware change.
body: Boards with a separate Wi-Fi chip can lose their connection shortly after starting ESPHome 2026.11.0 when that chip still runs firmware older than 2.12.0. Jonathan Swoboda corrects the handling of incoming data; an M5Stack Tab5 answered all 1,500 test pings, compared with 389 before the connection stopped in the comparison build.

A related change prevents startup from resetting the board before a recovery update can run. Smaller radio-firmware builds also fit the update space on ESP32-C6 and C61 chips that shipped with the older layout.

ESP32-C5 owners get a warning before an update between firmware families that use different storage layouts. That mismatch can leave the radio chip unable to start and require recovery over a direct serial connection. The warning does not block the update or identify which layout is actually on the chip.

articles.title: A watch complication no longer downloads the whole home
articles.dek: Android widgets, quick settings and Wear OS controls request the readings they actually display.
body: Refreshing one small watch-face display could fetch every device state and the complete entity registry from Home Assistant—several megabytes on a large installation. Filtering on the server reduces that request to the selected state and its registry entry.

The same approach reaches widgets, quick settings tiles, the Wear OS thermostat tile, media sessions and device controls. Lists that need a whole category request that category instead; older servers keep a compatible fallback.

articles.title: Music reaches the HomePods attached to your Apple TV
articles.dek: The room becomes one player; existing automations may need the replacement for its separate speaker entities.
body: Sending music to an Apple TV configured to use HomePods as its speakers could leave the room silent. Music Assistant sends audio directly to those HomePods while the television box shows the track and provides remote controls.

The room can join Sendspin groups, and “Play on HomePods only” avoids waking the Apple TV. Once the devices confirm that they belong together, their old separate HomePod players and Home Assistant entities are removed. The room keeps the Apple TV player’s settings and queue.

articles.title: Press the button without racing back to the setup screen
articles.dek: A blinking status light helps identify the device during migration, and authorization completes without another click.
body: The old HomeWizard authorization step allowed 30 seconds to press a physical button and submit a form. Home Assistant’s setup and reauthorization flows instead wait in the background and continue when access is granted, offering another attempt after five minutes.

The migration repair uses the same wait. On devices that support identification, a blinking light points to the correct socket or meter and stops when authorization finishes, the wait expires or the repair closes. Nathan van Ofwegen makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the setup change.

articles.title: Tell whether your Tile tracker is at home over Bluetooth
articles.dek: Account sign-in identifies your own trackers during setup; day-to-day presence uses nearby radio advertisements.
body: A tracker stays home while its Bluetooth advertisements reach Home Assistant and becomes away when they stop. The new Tile BLE integration listens locally, independently of the separate cloud integration.

Setup is started manually so a neighbour’s tracker does not generate an invitation. A one-time Tile account sign-in finds names and device keys; only the selected tracker’s key is stored, not the account credentials.

articles.title: Firmware installation gets past a stuck ZWA-2
articles.dek: The toolbox handles end-device firmware and gives a clear recovery step when a repeater fails to restart.
body: A Connect ZWA-2 already running end-device firmware could resist a fresh installation because the toolbox used the wrong route into its firmware installer. @AlCalzone enables the supported command, verified with a successful installation on a ZWA-2.

A related Z-Wave JS correction recognizes the installer when its startup message arrives in separate fragments. If a repeater still fails to restart, the toolbox stops before configuration and asks the owner to unplug and reconnect it, instead of reporting a misleading region error.

articles.title: Faster Lithuanian recognition on a local server
articles.dek: An optional language-specific engine cuts the delay in desktop tests; ordinary Whisper installations keep their existing path.
body: Short Lithuanian commands can use a recognizer that processes the audio received instead of Whisper’s fixed-length window. Wyoming Faster Whisper selects the LT_ausys model, based on Datolabs’ Upelis, when its optional onnx-asr speech engine is installed.

In the contributor’s 127-command test on a Ryzen computer, median recognition time was 0.18 seconds, compared with 3.55 seconds for the tested Paprika Whisper model. The recordings came from one speaker. This changes the standalone server package; it does not establish availability through the Home Assistant OS Whisper app.

articles.title: Defective QR labels no longer block thermostat pairing
articles.dek: The workaround is limited to a manufacturing error on some Heatit Z-TRM6 labels.
body: A stray decimal suffix on some factory labels makes SmartStart reject the code used to add a Heatit Z-TRM6 thermostat. @AMThie makes a first contribution to Z-Wave JS with a narrowly scoped correction for the defect confirmed by Heatit.
The original label’s checksum is still checked and the device’s security key is untouched. Incomplete identifying data remains invalid.

articles.title: Give a running timer more time than it started with
articles.dek: An extension affects the current countdown; the configured duration returns when it finishes or is cancelled.
body: Ten minutes into a 45-minute countdown, adding another 15 minutes used to be rejected because 50 minutes would remain. Home Assistant’s timer change action removes that ceiling.
The displayed duration grows when needed so progress stays within 100 percent. The safeguard against leaving a negative amount of time remains.

articles.title: Name that tune, one letter at a time
articles.dek: Early correct answers earn more points, with an optional extra guess for the artist.
body: As a song plays, blank spaces in its title gradually reveal letters. The new Title Reveal game in Music Quiz lets each player type guesses on their own device, then try the artist after solving the title.
Hosts choose the number of rounds, answer time, hint speed and typo tolerance. Spaces and punctuation stay visible, and guesses ignore differences such as accents and capitalization.

articles.title: Edit Jellyfin playlists from the music player
articles.dek: Permissions still apply, and removing one repeated track leaves its other copies in place.
body: Playlists owned by the connected Jellyfin account, or shared with editing permission, appear in Music Assistant’s “Add to playlist” instead of being treated as read-only. Tracks can also be removed without opening Jellyfin separately.

Removing a track targets that particular playlist entry, so another copy of the same song survives. Creating playlists and changing their order are outside this addition. If the server cannot verify editing permission, it leaves the playlist readable but read-only.
